sections.heading: 1. Official Prize Structure & Winning Tier Distribution (1:00 PM Draw)
sections.content:
The 14 September 2026 1:00 PM Dear Morning draw features a multi-tiered statutory prize structure crafted to distribute substantial prize amounts across both jackpot series and lower-denomination endings:

• 1st Prize: ₹1,00,00,000 (1 Winner: Ticket 73D 61419)
• Consolation Prize: ₹1,000 (Awarded to all other alphabetic series holding the matching 5-digit number)
• 2nd Prize: ₹9,000 (10 Winners across designated 5-digit serials)
• 3rd Prize: ₹450 (10 Winners across designated 4-digit serials)
• 4th Prize: ₹250 (10 Winners across designated 4-digit serials)
• 5th Prize: ₹120 (50 to 100 Winners across designated 4-digit serials)

Each ticket is priced at ₹6 (MRP) as approved by the finance department of the host state government. The draw was conducted in front of a panel of independent government-appointed judges.

sections.heading: 2. Step-by-Step Ticket Verification: How the Matching Logic Operates
sections.content:
To ensure complete clarity and eliminate common misunderstandings when cross-referencing newspaper sheets:

1. First Prize Matching: Requires an identical match of BOTH the 2-digit serial prefix (e.g., 84B) and the 5-digit sequential number.
2. Consolation Prize: If your ticket carries the same 5-digit sequence but has a different series letter, you are entitled to the ₹1,000 consolation reward.
3. 2nd Through 5th Tier: Winnings in these brackets are determined by matching the 4-digit or 5-digit terminal digits regardless of alphabetical series.

We strongly recommend that ticket holders do not mark, puncture, or apply adhesive tape to their tickets, as unblemished preservation is mandatory for official forensic inspection.

sections.heading: 3. Statutory Legal Claim Procedure: Counters, Windows & KYC Checklist
sections.content:
Should your ticket match any prize bracket in today's official notification, follow the legal claim workflow:

• Claim Window: Under the State Lottery Rules, claims must be lodged within 30 (thirty) calendar days from the date of gazette publication.
• For Rewards Below ₹10,000: Winners can claim instant disbursement through authorized retail lottery agents and stockists upon surrendering the winning ticket.
• For Jackpots and Prizes Above ₹10,000: The claim must be filed directly with the Directorate of State Lotteries or authorized nodal banks. Required documentation:
  - Original untampered lottery ticket signed by the winner on the reverse side.
  - Official Claim Application Form filled and signed in duplicate.
  - Four notarized passport-size photographs of the claimant.
  - Self-attested clear photocopies of PAN Card and Aadhaar Card.
  - Cancelled cheque leaf or bank passbook copy bearing the claimant's name and IFSC code for direct RTGS/NEFT settlement.
  - Non-judicial stamp paper affidavit verifying genuine non-transferred ownership.

sections.heading: 4. Comprehensive Tax Analysis: Section 194B Flat 30% TDS Mandate
sections.content:
All earnings derived from lotteries, crossword puzzles, and races are strictly categorized as 'Income from Other Sources' under Section 56(2)(ib) of the Indian Income Tax Act, 1961, and governed by Section 115BB and Section 194B:

• Mandatory Flat 30% TDS: Any prize payout exceeding ₹10,000 attracts a mandatory 30% tax deduction at source.
• Health & Education Cess: A 4% cess is charged on the TDS amount, resulting in an effective deduction rate of 31.20%.
• Gross ₹1,00,00,000 (₹1 Crore) Bumper Breakdown:
  - Basic TDS (30%): ₹30,00,000
  - Surcharge & Cess (4% on Tax): ₹1,20,000
  - Total Tax Deducted at Source: ₹31,20,000
  - Net Bank Credit to Winner: ₹68,80,000
• Prohibition of Losses or Deductions: Under Section 58(4), no expenditure, Chapter VI-A deductions (such as Section 80C, 80D), or basic income tax slab exemptions can be claimed against lottery income. The organizing state department furnishes Form 16A certifying tax remittance to the central exchequer.
